transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Oh, hello Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me... I really hope I'm not taking up time you need for other people. My family insisted I come in today. 

I've just been... well, I don't want you to think I'm a bad person, I really try to do right by people, but... I just keep telling my family that I'm the reason my friend passed away. I... I didn't call her back when I should have. And I had some... just some really ugly thoughts sometimes, which I'm so ashamed to even admit to you. 

It's my fault, and I know the Lord is punishing everybody at our church because of me. I'm sorry, I know that must sound terrible... is it okay that I share that with you? I just feel so awful about it all, and I hope you don't think too poorly of me.
Can you tell me more about these thoughts that make you feel guilty?

Oh... well, I really hope you won't judge me too harshly. I try so hard to be a good Christian woman, I really do. But... like I was saying, I just know I'm the reason she's gone. If I had just picked up the phone and called her back that afternoon... but I didn't. And sometimes I would get a little impatient with her, which are those awful, ugly thoughts I mentioned. Just selfish, wicked things. And now she's dead because of it. 

I'm just... I'm so useless, and I've brought this terrible ruin on her. And it doesn't even stop with her. The folks at our church... I just know in my heart that the Lord is punishing the whole congregation right now just because I'm there sitting among them. Because of what I did, and what a bad person I am. 

I'm so sorry, doctor, I know it's a terrible thing to admit. Are you... are you sure it's alright that I'm telling you all this? I really don't want to upset you.
Do you find yourself constantly thinking about these ugly thoughts, even when you try to focus on other things?

Oh... well, I don't think it's quite like that. I really do try my best to keep busy, you know? When I'm down at the store working the register, I make sure to just smile and focus on the customers. I'd hate to let my own... my own bad nature get in the way of doing a good job for them. 

So if I'm ringing someone up or doing my chores at home, I can usually keep my mind on what's right in front of me. I'm not... I'm not completely out of my head, I promise. I hope that's the right kind of answer. Is it okay that I can still focus on my work sometimes? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
Do you really believe that the Lord is punishing your church congregation because of you?

Oh, dear... I know how that must sound. I really don't want you to think I'm... well, that I'm losing my mind or making everything about myself. I try so hard to just sit quietly and be a good congregant. But... yes, I do believe it. 

It's... well, it's just that when I'm sitting there in the pews, and the pastor is saying the prayers... or when the choir sings certain lines in the hymns... I just know. I know they're really warning me. It's like a message that God has marked me, and that the whole church is suffering because I brought this terrible thing on us all. 

I'm so ashamed to even say it out loud to you. I hope you don't think I'm a dreadful person for bringing such a burden on those good people... or that I'm silly for noticing the warnings in the songs. Is it okay that I'm telling you this? I just want to be completely honest with you, like you asked, and I hope I'm explaining it the right way.
Do you feel like you're unable to control these thoughts about being responsible for your friend's death?

Oh, no, I... I wouldn't want you to think I'm completely out of control. I really do try to be strong, I promise. Like I mentioned with the store, I can usually push them aside when I need to be helpful to others. It's not like I'm just letting my mind run wild... I know that wouldn't be very proper. 

So, I don't think I'm unable to control them, exactly. It's just that when I'm alone, and it's quiet, the truth of what I did just sort of sits there with me. But I try my absolute best to keep a handle on it when I need to. 

Is... is that okay? I hope I'm answering your question right, doctor. I just really don't want you to think I'm not trying my hardest to be good.
Do you think these thoughts about being responsible for your friend's death and the church being punished are facts or just feelings?

Oh, well... I know it sounds like something a person would just imagine if they were feeling very low. And I really don't want you to think I'm making things up or being dramatic. I know I shouldn't let my imagination run away with me. 

But... oh, doctor, they really are facts to me. I don't want to sound stubborn, but like I was trying to explain before... when I'm sitting there in church, and the pastor is leading the prayers, or the choir is singing those specific lines... I just know it in my bones. It's not just a feeling. It's a real warning that God has marked me, and that I've brought all this suffering on the church. 

I'm so sorry if that's not the answer you were hoping for. I know a good person wouldn't have these kinds of terrible facts attached to them. Do you... do you think I'm being unreasonable for believing what I hear in the hymns? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the honest truth, even if it's ugly.
Do these thoughts about your friend's death and the church being punished keep coming back to you, even when you don't want to think about them?

Oh... well, I hope I'm understanding you correctly, doctor. I really don't want you to think I just let my mind wander off whenever it pleases, or that I'm not trying to be strong. I try to be very disciplined about things. 

So... no, I wouldn't say they keep coming back when I'm trying not to think about them. When I'm at the register at work, I make sure to keep my focus right there on the customers. I don't let those awful thoughts interrupt me when I have a job to do. I know that wouldn't be very professional. It's really only when the day is done, and I'm sitting quietly at home or in the pews... the thoughts are just sort of already there waiting for me. But they don't force their way in when I'm busy and don't want them there. 

Is... is that what you meant? I hope that's a helpful answer. I'm trying my very best to explain it properly for you, I just don't want you to think I'm completely helpless against my own mind.
Do you think you would still feel responsible for your friend's death if someone else told you it wasn't your fault?

Oh, well... that's a very kind thought, doctor. I know my friends and family mean well when they try to comfort me. And I always make sure to thank them, I really do. I don't want to seem ungrateful or difficult when people are just trying to be nice. 

But... oh, I hope this doesn't make me sound terribly stubborn. It's just that... well, like I was trying to explain about the church services. When the pastor is saying the prayers, or the choir is singing those specific lines... it's not just a feeling I can be talked out of. I know they're warning me. I know God has marked me, and that all the suffering in the church is because of what I brought on us. 

So, even if someone tells me it's not my fault, I... I still know the truth of it. It's right there in the hymns and the prayers. I'm so sorry, I know that's probably not what you want to hear. I really do try to listen to reason, I promise. Do you... do you think less of me because I can't just accept it when people tell me I'm not to blame? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you think the messages you hear in the hymns and prayers are meant for anyone else, or only for you?

Oh... well, I hope it doesn't sound selfish of me to say this. I know the church is a place for everyone, and the services are meant to comfort the whole congregation. I really don't want you to think I'm the kind of person who believes everything revolves around her. I know better than that.

But... when it comes to those specific moments... oh, doctor, I've tried so hard to convince myself it's just a general sermon. But when the pastor says certain prayers, or the choir sings those specific lines... I just know, deep down, that they aren't meant for the person sitting next to me. They are really warning *me*. It's a message that God has marked me, and that the church is suffering because of what I brought on us. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds terrible. I know a good Christian shouldn't think the service is singling them out for punishment. Do you... do you think I'm being arrogant for feeling like those warnings are just for me? I just want to make sure I'm answering you properly, even if it makes me look bad.
Do you think there's any possibility that the messages you hear in the hymns and prayers might be interpreted differently by someone else?

Oh... well, yes, I suppose they must. I'm sure if you or anyone else were sitting in the pew next to me, you'd just hear a normal, beautiful service. I really try to be reasonable about this, doctor, I promise. I know other people probably just hear the regular scripture, and I don't want you to think I expect everyone else to be caught up in my troubles. That would be terribly self-centered of me.

But... well, even if someone else interprets it as just a regular hymn, it doesn't change what I know is happening to me. When the pastor is up there saying those prayers, or the choir sings those certain lines... I just know they are really warning me. Even if the person next to me hears a message of comfort, the message I'm getting is that God has marked me, and that the church is suffering because I brought this on us. 

I'm so sorry, I know I keep saying the same awful things, and I really don't want to frustrate you. I know other people hear something different, but the warning is just so clear to me. Am... am I explaining that alright? I hope I'm giving you the answers you need, doctor.
Do you think it's possible that the messages you hear in the hymns and prayers are just your own interpretation and not actually meant to be warnings from God?

Oh, doctor... I really wish I could say yes. I truly do. I know how it must sound to you, and I don't want to be difficult or seem like I'm not trying to see reason. I know it would be so much better, so much easier, if it were just my own mind playing tricks on me. I've prayed for that to be the case, I really have.

But... oh, I hope you won't be disappointed in me for saying this... when I'm sitting there, and the pastor says those specific prayers, or the choir sings those certain lines... it's just not something I'm making up in my head. I can feel it. I know they are really warning me. It's as clear as day that God has marked me, and all the suffering happening in our church... it's because I brought this on us. 

I'm so sorry, I know I must sound completely unreasonable. I really don't mean to be. I just... I can't deny what I know is happening, even though I desperately wish it were just my own bad interpretation. Do you... do you understand why I can't just brush it off as my own thoughts? I hope I'm not making you upset by being so stubborn about this.
Do you think anyone else shares your belief that the church is being punished because of you?

Oh... well... I don't think anyone else would ever say it out loud. The people at my church are so kind, so forgiving. They would never want to point fingers or make an old woman feel bad. I don't want you to think my congregation is cruel, doctor, they really aren't. They are wonderful people. 

But... well, I see how they look at me sometimes. And even if they don't say it to my face, I know they hear the same things I do. When the pastor says those prayers, or the choir sings those specific lines... they have to know what it means, right? They hear the warnings just like I do. They know God has marked me. They might smile at me after the service, but deep down, they have to know that the church is suffering because of what I brought on us. 

I'm sorry, I know it's terrible of me to assume what other people are thinking. I really try not to be one of those people who puts words in others' mouths. It's just... it's just so heavy, carrying this around. Do you... do you think I'm awful for believing they know it's my fault? I hope I'm not giving you a bad impression of me or my church.

It's just... it's just so heavy, carrying this around. Do you... do you think I'm awful for believing they know it's my fault? I hope I'm not giving you a bad impression of me or my church.
